Extensions are programs integrated with HyperWorks to enhance or extend the user experience. Altair Binary Format (ABF) is the standard binary format read by the program. A library called abflib allows you to create files in ABF. A generic ASCII reader is now available which allows you to bring custom results directly into HyperView. The Altair ASCII format is useful for reading the results of any in-house or propriety codes which are saved in a generic format. Batch mode allows you perform a series of operations outside the program interface. External resources can be registered in preference files, session files, or Templex files. If an external resource is registered in a program session, it is automatically registered in the session file when the session is saved. Translators are utilities that are run from the command line of the operating system to convert various types of files into different formats. Learn the basics and discover the workspace.Discover HyperWorks Desktop functionality with interactive tutorials. Start HyperWorks Desktop and configure the applications. Create, open, import, and save models. Control the view and display of your model in the modeling window. Use the Session Browser to view the current session and all the pages and windows it contains in a hierarchical display. Publish your HyperWorks Desktop session to HTML, PowerPoint, or Report files. Use the Parameters Browser to parameterize the contents of a session file or report template and automate a variety of analysis processes. Automate common workflows using the Process Manager. Explore, organize and manage your personal data, collaborate in teams, and connect to other data sources, such as corporate PLM systems to access CAD data or publish simulation data. Overview of external readers and the Altair Binary Format, the generic ASCII reader, running HyperWorks in batch mode, using Tcl/Tk commands, translators, and result math. Extensions are programs integrated with HyperWorks to enhance or extend the user experience. Altair Binary Format (ABF) is the standard binary format read by the program. A library called abflib allows you to create files in ABF. A generic ASCII reader is now available which allows you to bring custom results directly into HyperView. The Altair ASCII format is useful for reading the results of any in-house or propriety codes which are saved in a generic format. Batch mode allows you perform a series of operations outside the program interface. External resources can be registered in preference files, session files, or Templex files. If an external resource is registered in a program session, it is automatically registered in the session file when the session is saved. The HyperWorks Desktop scripting interface is a set of Tcl/Tk commands that follow a simple and consistent syntax. Translators are utilities that are run from the command line of the operating system to convert various types of files into different formats. Overview of external readers and the Altair Binary Format, the generic ASCII reader, running HyperWorks in batch mode, using Tcl/Tk commands, translators, and result math. Extensions are programs integrated with HyperWorks to enhance or extend the user experience. Altair Binary Format (ABF) is the standard binary format read by the program. A library called abflib allows you to create files in ABF. A generic ASCII reader is now available which allows you to bring custom results directly into HyperView. The Altair ASCII format is useful for reading the results of any in-house or propriety codes which are saved in a generic format. Batch mode allows you perform a series of operations outside the program interface. External resources can be registered in preference files, session files, or Templex files. If an external resource is registered in a program session, it is automatically registered in the session file when the session is saved. The HyperWorks Desktop scripting interface is a set of Tcl/Tk commands that follow a simple and consistent syntax. Translators are utilities that are run from the command line of the operating system to convert various types of files into different formats. XML commands in the Result Math Module.Record playback workflows in HyperView. These provide an overview of all additions, updates, and changes to the HyperMesh APIs for each release. A library called abflib allows you to create files in ABF. A generic ASCII reader is now available which allows you to bring custom results directly into HyperView. The Altair ASCII format is useful for reading the results of any in-house or propriety codes which are saved in a generic format. Batch mode allows you perform a series of operations outside the program interface. External resources can be registered in preference files, session files, or Templex files. Extensions are programs integrated with HyperWorks to enhance or extend the user experience. Altair Binary Format (ABF) is the standard binary format read by the program. A library called abflib allows you to create files in ABF. A generic ASCII reader is now available which allows you to bring custom results directly into HyperView. The Altair ASCII format is useful for reading the results of any in-house or propriety codes which are saved in a generic format. Batch mode allows you perform a series of operations outside the program interface. External resources can be registered in preference files, session files, or Templex files. Details on the HMASCII format and associated commands. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the curve (must be unique). name The name of the curve. title The title of the curve. xkind xpath xtype xreg xcomp ykind ypath ytype yreg ycomp linetype The line style used to draw the curve line. Must be one of the following values: 0 - no line 1 - solid line 2 - pattern1 3 - pattern2 4 - pattern3 5 - pattern4 markertype The marker type used to draw points on the curve. Must be one of the following values: 0 - no marker 1 - circle marker 2 - triangle marker 3 - square marker color The color of the curve. Refer to the color variable chart. width The width of the curve line in pixels (either 1 or 3). scalex The x axis scale factor. scaley The y axis scale factor. |

This must follow *component(). The element will be assigned to the most recent component created using *component(). Nodes must also be defined using *node() before creating an element using those nodes. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the element. type The solver specific element type. node1 The ID of the first node. node2 The ID of the second node. node3 The ID of the third node. node4 The ID of the fourth node. node5 The ID of the fifth node. node6 The ID of the sixth node. node7 The ID of the seventh node. node8 The ID of the eighth node. node9 The ID of the ninth node. node10 The ID of the tenth node. node11 The ID of the eleventh node. node12 The ID of the twelfth node. node13 The ID of the thirteenth node. node14 The ID of the fourteenth node. node15 The ID of the fifteenth node. node16 The ID of the sixteenth node. node17 The ID of the seventeenth node. node18 The ID of the eighteenth node. node19 The ID of the nineteenth node. node20 The ID of the twentieth node. propertyid The ID of the property directly assigned to the element. If specified as 0, the property is taken from the component. |
| [*hexa8()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_hexa8.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*hexa8 (id,type,node1,node2,node3,node4,node5,node6,node7,node8,propertyid)` | Creates a hexa8 element in HMASCII format. This must follow *component(). The element will be assigned to the most recent component created using *component(). Nodes must also be defined using *node() before creating an element using those nodes. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the element. type The solver specific element type. node1 The ID of the first node. node2 The ID of the second node. node3 The ID of the third node. node4 The ID of the fourth node. node5 The ID of the fifth node. node6 The ID of the sixth node. node7 The ID of the seventh node. node8 The ID of the eighth node. propertyid The ID of the property directly assigned to the element. If specified as 0, the property is taken from the component. |
| [*hm_features()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_hm_features.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*hm_features (id,"name",color)` | Creates a feature in HMASCII format. Additional attribute or dataname information is provided separately, see referenced commands. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the feature. name The name of the feature. color The color of the feature. Valid values are 1-64. |
| [*hourglass()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_hourglass.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*hourglass() (id, name,color)` | Creates an hourglass in HMASCII format. Additional attribute or dataname information is provided separately, see referenced commands. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the hourglass. name The name of the hourglass. color The color of the hourglass. Valid values are 1-64. |
| [*ice()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_ice.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*ice (id,type,independentnodesmax,dependentnodesmax)` | Creates an IC element in HMASCII format. This must follow *component(). The element will be assigned to the most recent component created using *component(). *icelink must be used to define the independent nodes. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the element. type The solver specific element type. independentnodesmax The number of independent nodes. dependentnodesmax The number of dependent nodes. |
| [*icelink()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_icelink.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*icelink (independentnodeid,dependentnodesmax,dependentnodeid_1,dependentdof_1,...,dependentnodeid_N,dependentnodedof_N)` | Defines the independent nodes for an IC element in HMASCII format. This must follow *ice(). The definition applies to the most recent IC created using *ice(). Nodes must also be defined using *node() before creating an element using those nodes. | **Inputs:** independentnodeid The ID of the independent node to add. dependentnodesmax The number of dependent nodes associated with the independent node. dependentnodeid_N The dependent node ID. This is repeated along with dependentnodedof_N for each dependent node. dependentnodedof_N The dependent node DOF. This is repeated along with dependentnodeid_N for each dependent node. |
| [*icoeffs()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_icoeffs.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*icoeffs (coeff1,coeff2,...,coeffN)` | Defines the independent nodes coefficients for an equation load. The *equation(), *inodes(), *idofs() and *icoeffs() blocks must be in the following order: *equation() *inodes() *idofs() *icoeffs() | **Inputs:** coeffs The coefficients of each independent node DOF. Each DOF has a coefficient, even if it is not active for that node (DOFs per node). So there are independentnodesmax*6 values. The order must match with the order of the independent nodes in the *inodes() command. |
| [*idofs()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_idofs.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*idofs (dofs1,dofs2,...,dofsN)` | Defines the independent nodes degrees of freedom for an equation load. The *equation(), *inodes(), *idofs() and *icoeffs() blocks must be in the following order: *equation() *inodes() *idofs() *icoeffs() | **Inputs:** dofs The degrees of freedom of each independent nodes. Each active DOF is appended to the string for that node. For example, DOFs 1,3 and 6 active results in 136. The order must match with the order of the independent nodes in the *inodes() command. |

| [*inodes()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_inodes.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*inodes (id1,id2,...,idN)` | Defines the independent nodes for an equation load. The *equation(), *inodes(), *idofs() and *icoeffs() blocks must be in the following order: *equation() *inodes() *idofs() *icoeffs() | **Inputs:** ids The IDs of the independent nodes. |
| [*integrationrules()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_integrationrules.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*integrationrules (id,name,color)` | Creates integrationrules in HMASCII format. Additional attribute or dataname information is provided separately, see referenced commands. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the integrationrules. name The name of the integrationrules. color The color of the integrationrules. Valid values are 1-64. |
| [*interfacecomponents()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_interfacecomponents.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*interfacecomponents (id,"name",color)` | Creates an interfacecomponent in HMASCII format. Additional attribute or dataname information is provided separately, see referenced commands. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the interfacecomponent. name The name of the interfacecomponent. color The color of the interfacecomponent. Valid values are 1-64. |
| [*interfacelinkings()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_interfacelinkings.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*interfacelinkings (id,"name",color)` | Creates an interfacelinking in HMASCII format. Additional attribute or dataname information is provided separately, see referenced commands. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the interfacelinking. name The name of the interfacelinking. color The color of the interfacelinking. Valid values are 1-64. |
| [*interfacepairlist()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_interfacepairlist.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*interfacepairlist (entity_ids)` | Defines the interface pairs for a sub-laminate laminate. | **Inputs:** entity_ids The IDs that define the interface pairs for a sub-laminate laminate, separated by commas. Each pair consists of two IDs. |
| [*interfacepairmax()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_interfacepairmax.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*interfacepairmax (count)` | Defines the number of interface pairs assigned to a sub-laminate laminate. | **Inputs:** count The number of interface pairs assigned to a sub-laminate laminate. |
| [*internalsupports()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_internalsupports.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*internalsupports (id,name,color)` | Creates an internalsupport in HMASCII format. Additional attribute or dataname information is provided separately, see referenced commands. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the internalsupport. name The name of the internalsupport. color The color of the internalsupport. Valid values are 1-64. |

Overview of external readers and the Altair Binary Format, the generic ASCII reader, running HyperWorks in batch mode, using Tcl/Tk commands, translators, and result math. Extensions are programs integrated with HyperWorks to enhance or extend the user experience. Altair Binary Format (ABF) is the standard binary format read by the program. A library called abflib allows you to create files in ABF. A generic ASCII reader is now available which allows you to bring custom results directly into HyperView. The Altair ASCII format is useful for reading the results of any in-house or propriety codes which are saved in a generic format. Batch mode allows you perform a series of operations outside the program interface. External resources can be registered in preference files, session files, or Templex files. If an external resource is registered in a program session, it is automatically registered in the session file when the session is saved. The HyperWorks Desktop scripting interface is a set of Tcl/Tk commands that follow a simple and consistent syntax. Translators are utilities that are run from the command line of the operating system to convert various types of files into different formats. Valid values are 1-64. |
| [*laminateidlist()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_laminateidlist.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*laminateidlist (entity_ids)` | Defines the plies or sub-laminates assigned to a ply laminate or sub-laminate laminate. | **Inputs:** entity_ids The IDs of the plies or sub-laminates assigned to a ply laminate or sub-laminate laminate, separated by commas. |
| [*laminateidlistmax()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_laminateidlistmax.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*laminateidlistmax (count)` | Defines the number of plies or sub-laminates assigned to a ply laminate or sub-laminate laminate. | **Inputs:** count The number of plies or sub-laminates assigned to a ply laminate or sub-laminate laminate. |
| [*laminates()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_laminates2.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*laminates (id,"name",color,convention,config,repeat)` | Creates a laminate in HMASCII format. To add plies, sub-laminates and interfaces to a laminate, use the *interfacepairlist(), *interfacepairmax(), *laminateidlist() and *laminateidlistmax() commands. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the laminate. name The name of the laminate. color The color of the laminate. Valid values are 1-64. convention The lamiante stacking convention. Valid values are: 0 - Total 1 - Membrane 2 - Bending 3 - Smear 4 - Smear core 5 - Symmetric 6 - Symmetric membrane 7 - Symmetric bending 8 - Symmetric smear config The config of the laminate. Valid values are: 0 - Ply laminate, which references plies. 1 - Sub-laminate laminate, which references sub-laminates and interfaces 2 - Sub-laminate, which references plies for the sub-laminate. repeat Currently ignored. Must be set to 0. |
| [*legends()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_legends.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*legends (id,name,color)` | Creates a legend in HMASCII format. Additional attribute or dataname information is provided separately, see referenced commands. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the legend. name The name of the legend. color The color of the legend. Valid values are 1-64. |
| [*lists()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_lists.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*lists (id, name, color)` | Creates a list in HMASCII format. Additional attribute or dataname information is provided separately, see referenced commands. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the list. name The name of the list. color The color of the list. Valid values are 1-64. |

| [*main3()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_main3.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*main3 (id,type,node1,node2,node3)` | Creates a main3 element in HMASCII format. This must follow *group(). The element will be assigned to the most recent group created using *component(). Nodes must also be defined using *node() before creating an element using those nodes. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the element. type The solver specific element type. node1 The ID of the first node. node2 The ID of the second node. node3 The ID of the third node. |
| [*main4()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_main4.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*main4 (id,type,node1,node2,node3,node4)` | Creates a main4 element in HMASCII format. This must follow *group(). The element will be assigned to the most recent group created using *component(). Nodes must also be defined using *node() before creating an element using those nodes. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the element. type The solver specific element type. node1 The ID of the first node. node2 The ID of the second node. node3 The ID of the third node. node4 The ID of the fourth node. |
| [*mass()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_mass.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*mass (id,type,node1,propertyid,systemid,mass)` | Creates a mass element in HMASCII format. This must follow *component(). The element will be assigned to the most recent component created using *component(). Nodes must also be defined using *node() before creating an element using those nodes. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the element. type The solver specific element type. node1 The ID of the first node. propertyid The ID of the property directly assigned to the element. If specified as 0, the property is taken from the component. systemid The ID of the system assigned to the element. If specified as 0, there is no assigned system. mass The mass of the element. |
| [*material()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_material.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*material (id,name,color)` | Creates a material in HMASCII format. Material data is assigned using attributes for the relevant solver. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the material. name The name of the material. color The color of the material. Valid values are 1-64. |
| [*materialbehaviors()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_materialbehaviors.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*materialbehaviors (id,name,color)` | Creates a material behavior in HMASCII format. Additional attribute or dataname information is provided separately, see referenced commands. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the material behavior. name The name of the material behavior. color The color of the material behavior. Valid values are 1-64. |
| [*mechanismconstraints()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_mechanismconstraints.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*mechanismconstraints (id,"name",color)` | Creates a mechanism constraint in HMASCII format. Valid values are 1-64. |

| [*penta15()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_penta15.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*penta15 (id,type,node1,node2,node3,node4,node5,node6,node7,node8,node9,node10,node11,node12,node13,node14,node15,propertyid)` | Creates a penta15 element in HMASCII format. This must follow *component(). The element will be assigned to the most recent component created using *component(). Nodes must also be defined using *node() before creating an element using those nodes. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the element. type The solver specific element type. node1 The ID of the first node. node2 The ID of the second node. node3 The ID of the third node. node4 The ID of the fourth node. node5 The ID of the fifth node. node6 The ID of the sixth node. node7 The ID of the seventh node. node8 The ID of the eighth node. node9 The ID of the ninth node. node10 The ID of the tenth node. node11 The ID of the eleventh node. node12 The ID of the twelfth node. node13 The ID of the thirteenth node. node14 The ID of the fourteenth node. node15 The ID of the fifteenth node. propertyid The ID of the property directly assigned to the element. If specified as 0, the property is taken from the component. |
| [*penta6()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_penta6.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*penta6 (id,type,node1,node2,node3,node4,node5,node6,propertyid)` | Creates a penta6 element in HMASCII format. This must follow *component(). The element will be assigned to the most recent component created using *component(). Nodes must also be defined using *node() before creating an element using those nodes. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the element. type The solver specific element type. node1 The ID of the first node. node2 The ID of the second node. node3 The ID of the third node. node4 The ID of the fourth node. node5 The ID of the fifth node. node6 The ID of the sixth node. propertyid The ID of the property directly assigned to the element. If specified as 0, the property is taken from the component. |

Additional attribute or dataname information is provided separately, see referenced commands. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the perturbations. name The name of the perturbations. color The color of the perturbations. Valid values are 1-64. |
| [*physicalquantities()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_physicalquantities.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*physicalquantities (id,"name",color)` | Creates a physicalquantity in HMASCII format. Valid values are 1-64. |
| [*plies()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_plies2.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*plies (id,"name",color,entity_type,material_id,thickness1,orient_angle,integration_points,result_request,thickness2,thickness3,thickness4,table_id)` | Creates a ply in HMASCII format. To add entities to a ply, use the *plyidlistmax() and *plyidlist() commands. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the ply. name The name of the ply. color The color of the ply. Valid values are 1-64. entity_type The type of the entity assigned to the ply. Valid values are sets. material_id The ID of the material assigned to the ply. thickness1 The thickness of the ply. orient_angle The orientation angle of the ply, in degrees. integration_points The number of integration points for the ply. result_request 0 - Do not output results. 1 - Output results. thickness2 The second thickness of the ply for solvers that support multiple thicknesses. thickness3 The third thickness of the ply for solvers that support multiple thicknesses. thickness4 The fourth thickness of the ply for solvers that support multiple thicknesses. table_id The ID of the table containing the drape information, valid only for OptiStruct. |

Use the Session Browser to view the current session and all the pages and windows it contains in a hierarchical display. Publish your HyperWorks Desktop session to HTML, PowerPoint, or Report files. Use the Parameters Browser to parameterize the contents of a session file or report template and automate a variety of analysis processes. Automate common workflows using the Process Manager. Explore, organize and manage your personal data, collaborate in teams, and connect to other data sources, such as corporate PLM systems to access CAD data or publish simulation data. Overview of external readers and the Altair Binary Format, the generic ASCII reader, running HyperWorks in batch mode, using Tcl/Tk commands, translators, and result math. Extensions are programs integrated with HyperWorks to enhance or extend the user experience. Altair Binary Format (ABF) is the standard binary format read by the program. A library called abflib allows you to create files in ABF. A generic ASCII reader is now available which allows you to bring custom results directly into HyperView. The Altair ASCII format is useful for reading the results of any in-house or propriety codes which are saved in a generic format. Batch mode allows you perform a series of operations outside the program interface. External resources can be registered in preference files, session files, or Templex files. If an external resource is registered in a program session, it is automatically registered in the session file when the session is saved. The HyperWorks Desktop scripting interface is a set of Tcl/Tk commands that follow a simple and consistent syntax. Translators are utilities that are run from the command line of the operating system to convert various types of files into different formats. Learn the basics and discover the workspace.Discover HyperWorks Desktop functionality with interactive tutorials. Start HyperWorks Desktop and configure the applications. Create, open, import, and save models. Control the view and display of your model in the modeling window. Use the Session Browser to view the current session and all the pages and windows it contains in a hierarchical display. Publish your HyperWorks Desktop session to HTML, PowerPoint, or Report files. Use the Parameters Browser to parameterize the contents of a session file or report template and automate a variety of analysis processes. Automate common workflows using the Process Manager. Explore, organize and manage your personal data, collaborate in teams, and connect to other data sources, such as corporate PLM systems to access CAD data or publish simulation data. Overview of external readers and the Altair Binary Format, the generic ASCII reader, running HyperWorks in batch mode, using Tcl/Tk commands, translators, and result math. Extensions are programs integrated with HyperWorks to enhance or extend the user experience. Altair Binary Format (ABF) is the standard binary format read by the program. A library called abflib allows you to create files in ABF. A generic ASCII reader is now available which allows you to bring custom results directly into HyperView. The Altair ASCII format is useful for reading the results of any in-house or propriety codes which are saved in a generic format. Batch mode allows you perform a series of operations outside the program interface. External resources can be registered in preference files, session files, or Templex files. If an external resource is registered in a program session, it is automatically registered in the session file when the session is saved. The HyperWorks Desktop scripting interface is a set of Tcl/Tk commands that follow a simple and consistent syntax. Translators are utilities that are run from the command line of the operating system to convert various types of files into different formats. XML commands in the Result Math Module.Record playback workflows in HyperView. These provide an overview of all additions, updates, and changes to the HyperMesh APIs for each release. Details on the core data that can be queried and manipulated.This API allows external applications to link HyperMesh as a library and provides a limited set of functions and structures to access specific functionality. FE input readers are C programs that read information from ASCII or binary finite element models files into the HyperMesh database. Create, open, import, and save models. Control the view and display of your model in the modeling window. Overview of external readers and the Altair Binary Format, the generic ASCII reader, running HyperWorks in batch mode, using Tcl/Tk commands, translators, and result math. Extensions are programs integrated with HyperWorks to enhance or extend the user experience. Altair Binary Format (ABF) is the standard binary format read by the program. A library called abflib allows you to create files in ABF. A generic ASCII reader is now available which allows you to bring custom results directly into HyperView. The Altair ASCII format is useful for reading the results of any in-house or propriety codes which are saved in a generic format. Batch mode allows you perform a series of operations outside the program interface. External resources can be registered in preference files, session files, or Templex files. If an external resource is registered in a program session, it is automatically registered in the session file when the session is saved. The HyperWorks Desktop scripting interface is a set of Tcl/Tk commands that follow a simple and consistent syntax. Translators are utilities that are run from the command line of the operating system to convert various types of files into different formats. Details on the HMASCII format and associated commands.Adds geometry to a rigid wall group in HMASCII format.Adds geometry to a rigid wall group in HMASCII format. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the group. geometrytype 1 - infinite plane 2 - finite plane 3 - infinite prism 4 - finite prism 5 - cylinder 6 - sphere For geometrytypes 1 and 2: xaxisx, xaxisy, xaxisz The x, y, z components describing the local x axis. lengthx, lengthy The local x and y length of the rigid wall. For geometrytypes 3 and 4: xaxisx, xaxisy, xaxisz The x, y, z components describing the local x axis. lengthx,lengthy,lengthz The local x, y and z length of the rigid wall. For geometrytype 5: radius The radius of the rigid wall. lengthz The length of the cylinder. For geometrytype 6: radius The radius of the sphere. For geomtrytypes 7 and 8: MADYMOID ID corresponding to the geometry description in the MADYMO deck. |

This must follow *systemcollector(). The system will be assigned to the most recent systemcollector created using *systemcollector(). | **Inputs:** id The ID of the system. type The type of system: 0 - rectangular 1 - cylindrical 2 - spherical inputsystemid The ID of the first node. xaxisx xaxisy xaxisz The x, y, z coordinates that make up the vector defining the x-direction of the system. Only used if definitioncode is 0. yaxisx yaxisy yaxisz The x, y, z coordinates that make up the vector defining the y-direction of the system. Only used if definitioncode is 0. zaxisx zaxisy zaxisz The x, y, z coordinates that make up the vector defining the z-direction of the system. Only used if definitioncode is 0. originx originy originz The x, y, z coordinates that make up the origin of the system. Only used if definitioncode is 0. originnodeid The ID of the origin node for a node-dependent system. Only used if definitioncode is not 0. axisnodeid The ID of the axis node for a node-dependent system. Only used if definitioncode is not 0. planenodeid The ID of the plane node for a node-dependent system. Only used if definitioncode is not 0. definitioncode The system code for a node-dependent system: 0 - Non-node-dependent system 1 - x-axis, xy-plane 2 - x-axis, xz-plane 3 - y-axis, xy-plane 4 - y-axis, yz-plane 5 - z-axis, yz-plane 6 - z-axis, xz-plane |

| [*tablecolumnlabels()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_tablecolumnlabels.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*tablecolumnlabels ("label1","label2",...,"labelN")` | Defines the column labels of a table in HMASCII format. | [*tablecolumnstart()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_tablecolumnstart.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*tablecolumnstart (index,entity_type,column_type)` | Starts the data definition of a column in a table in HMASCII format. Valid values are: 1 - integer 2 - unsigned integer/entity ID 3 - float 4 - double 5 - bool 6 - string 7 - triple |
| [*tablecolumntypes()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_tablecolumntypes.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*tablecolumntypes (type1,type2,...,typeN)` | Defines the column types of a table in HMASCII format. Extensions are programs integrated with HyperWorks to enhance or extend the user experience. Altair Binary Format (ABF) is the standard binary format read by the program. A library called abflib allows you to create files in ABF. A generic ASCII reader is now available which allows you to bring custom results directly into HyperView. The Altair ASCII format is useful for reading the results of any in-house or propriety codes which are saved in a generic format. Batch mode allows you perform a series of operations outside the program interface. External resources can be registered in preference files, session files, or Templex files. If an external resource is registered in a program session, it is automatically registered in the session file when the session is saved. Translators are utilities that are run from the command line of the operating system to convert various types of files into different formats. | [*transformations()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_transformations.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*transformations (id,"name",color)` | Creates a transformation in HMASCII format. Additional attribute or dataname information is provided separately, see referenced commands. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the transformation. name The name of the transformation. color The color of the transformation. Valid values are 1-64. |
| [*tria3()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_tria3.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*tria3 (id,type,node1,node2,node3,propertyid)` | Creates a tria3 element in HMASCII format. This must follow *component(). The element will be assigned to the most recent component created using *component(). Nodes must also be defined using *node() before creating an element using those nodes. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the element. type The solver specific element type. node1 The ID of the first node. node2 The ID of the second node. node3 The ID of the third node. propertyid The ID of the property directly assigned to the element. If specified as 0, the property is taken from the component. |
| [*tria6()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_tria6.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*tria6 (id,type,node1,node2,node3,node4,node5,node6,propertyid)` | Creates a tria6 element in HMASCII format. This must follow *component(). The element will be assigned to the most recent component created using *component(). Nodes must also be defined using *node() before creating an element using those nodes. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the element. type The solver specific element type. node1 The ID of the first node. node2 The ID of the second node. node3 The ID of the third node. node4 The ID of the fourth node. node5 The ID of the fifth node. node6 The ID of the sixth node. propertyid The ID of the property directly assigned to the element. If specified as 0, the property is taken from the component. |
| [*valuesforentity()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_valuesforentity.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*valuesforentity (entity_type,entity_id,number_of_values)` | Defines a data names block for new-style HyperMesh entities in HMASCII format. | **Inputs:** entity_type The type of entity for which the data names are being defined. Only new-style entities are supported. id The ID of the entity for which the data names are being defined. number_of_values The number of data names that follow. |

Overview of external readers and the Altair Binary Format, the generic ASCII reader, running HyperWorks in batch mode, using Tcl/Tk commands, translators, and result math. Extensions are programs integrated with HyperWorks to enhance or extend the user experience. Altair Binary Format (ABF) is the standard binary format read by the program. A library called abflib allows you to create files in ABF. A generic ASCII reader is now available which allows you to bring custom results directly into HyperView. The Altair ASCII format is useful for reading the results of any in-house or propriety codes which are saved in a generic format. Batch mode allows you perform a series of operations outside the program interface. External resources can be registered in preference files, session files, or Templex files. If an external resource is registered in a program session, it is automatically registered in the session file when the session is saved. The HyperWorks Desktop scripting interface is a set of Tcl/Tk commands that follow a simple and consistent syntax. Translators are utilities that are run from the command line of the operating system to convert various types of files into different formats. Overview of external readers and the Altair Binary Format, the generic ASCII reader, running HyperWorks in batch mode, using Tcl/Tk commands, translators, and result math. Details on the HMASCII format and associated commands. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the element (must be unique). type The element type. locationid The node ID where the load is applied. inputsystemid The reference coordinate system of the load (must be a valid system or 0). comp1 The x component of the load. comp2 The y component of the load. comp3 The z component of the load. |
| [*weld()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_weld2.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*weld (id,type,node1,node2,dof)` | Creates a weld element in HMASCII format. This must follow *component(). The element will be assigned to the most recent component created using *component(). Nodes must also be defined using *node() before creating an element using those nodes. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the element. type The solver specific element type. node1 The ID of the first node. node2 The ID of the second node. dof The DOF (1-6) of the element. |
| [*weldlines()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_weldlines.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*weldlines (id,"name",color)` | Creates a weldline in HMASCII format. Additional attribute or dataname information is provided separately, see referenced commands. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the weldline. name The name of the weldline. color The color of the weldline. Valid values are 1-64. |
| [*xelem()](https://2022.help.altair.com/2022.3/hwdesktop/hwd/topics/reference/hm/_xelem_2.htm) | HyperMesh HMASCII Command | `*xelem (id,type,dependentnodeset,dependentnodesmax)` | Creates an xelem element in HMASCII format. This must follow *component(). The element will be assigned to the most recent component created using *component(). A *dependentnodes() description must immediately follow. Nodes must also be defined using *node() before creating an element using those nodes. | **Inputs:** id The ID of the element. type The solver specific element type. dependentnodeset The ID of the dependent node set. dependentnodexmax The number of dependent nodes in the set. |
